```{r setup, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE)
library(tidyverse)

v2_dir <- "results_cache"
dir.create(v2_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(v2_dir, "models"), showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(v2_dir, "derived"), showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(v2_dir, "data"), showWarnings = FALSE)

# Reuse a local World Bank snapshot on recompilation. Set this to TRUE to refresh.
refresh_worldbank_gdp <- FALSE
wb_country_path <- file.path(v2_dir, "data", "worldbank-country-codes.csv")
wb_gdp_path <- file.path(v2_dir, "data", "worldbank-gdp-per-capita.csv")
wb_meta_path <- file.path(v2_dir, "data", "worldbank-gdp-provenance.csv")
if (refresh_worldbank_gdp || !all(file.exists(c(wb_country_path, wb_gdp_path, wb_meta_path)))) {
  wb_country_url <- "https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country?format=json&per_page=400"
  wb_gdp_url <- paste0(
    "https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/all/indicator/NY.GDP.PCAP.CD",
    "?format=json&per_page=20000&MRV=1"
  )
  wb_country_json <- jsonlite::fromJSON(wb_country_url, simplifyVector = FALSE)
  wb_gdp_json <- jsonlite::fromJSON(wb_gdp_url, simplifyVector = FALSE)
  wb_country_codes <- purrr::map_dfr(wb_country_json[[2]], function(x) {
    tibble(iso2 = x$iso2Code, iso3 = x$id, country_worldbank = x$name)
  }) %>%
    filter(!is.na(iso2), nzchar(iso2), !is.na(iso3), nzchar(iso3)) %>%
    distinct(iso2, .keep_all = TRUE)
  wb_gdp_snapshot <- purrr::map_dfr(wb_gdp_json[[2]], function(x) {
    tibble(
      iso2 = x$country$id,
      country_worldbank = x$country$value,
      GDP_year = suppressWarnings(as.integer(x$date)),
      GDP_per_capita_current_USD = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x$value))
    )
  }) %>%
    filter(!is.na(iso2), is.finite(GDP_per_capita_current_USD)) %>%
    arrange(iso2, desc(GDP_year)) %>%
    group_by(iso2) %>% slice_head(n = 1) %>% ungroup() %>%
    left_join(wb_country_codes %>% select(iso2, iso3), by = "iso2") %>%
    filter(!is.na(iso3))
  readr::write_csv(wb_country_codes, wb_country_path)
  readr::write_csv(wb_gdp_snapshot, wb_gdp_path)
  readr::write_csv(tibble(
    retrieved_on = as.character(Sys.Date()),
    indicator = "NY.GDP.PCAP.CD",
    indicator_label = "GDP per capita (current US$)",
    selection = "Most recent non-missing annual observation per country",
    country_api = wb_country_url,
    indicator_api = wb_gdp_url
  ), wb_meta_path)
}
wb_country_codes <- readr::read_csv(wb_country_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
wb_gdp_snapshot <- readr::read_csv(wb_gdp_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
wb_provenance <- readr::read_csv(wb_meta_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

v2_inputs <- c("all_withNorway_noTest_countryFill_raw.csv", "GCI.csv",
               wb_country_path, wb_gdp_path, wb_meta_path)
v2_packages <- c("knitr", "lme4", "mgcv", "gamm4", "lavaan", "dplyr",
                 "tidyr", "ggplot2", "gt", "broom", "broom.mixed", "psych",
                 "kableExtra", "jsonlite", "patchwork", "sjPlot", "mlisi",
                 "digest")
v2_signature <- digest::digest(list(
  tools::md5sum(v2_inputs), R.version.string,
  setNames(lapply(v2_packages, function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p))), v2_packages)
))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache = TRUE, cache.lazy = FALSE,
  cache.path = file.path(v2_dir, paste0("knitr-", knitr::opts_knit$get("rmarkdown.pandoc.to"), "/")),
  fig.path = "results_files/figure-", error = FALSE)
set.seed(20261016)

# Hash the CURRENT upstream R code on every render, not the prose or captions.
# This propagates changes to data preparation and helper functions downstream.
v2_lines <- readLines(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE), warn = FALSE)
v2_starts <- grep("^```\\{r", v2_lines)
v2_code_keys <- character(length(v2_starts))
v2_labels <- character(length(v2_starts))
v2_unnamed <- 0L
v2_previous <- "results-code-v1"
for (i in seq_along(v2_starts)) {
  start <- v2_starts[i]
  end <- start + which(v2_lines[(start + 1L):length(v2_lines)] == "```")[1]
  code <- v2_lines[(start + 1L):(end - 1L)]
  header <- sub("^```\\{r", "", v2_lines[start])
  header <- sub("\\}$", "", header)
  label <- trimws(strsplit(header, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]][1])
  yaml_label <- grep("^#\\| label:", code, value = TRUE)
  if (length(yaml_label)) label <- trimws(sub("^#\\| label:", "", yaml_label[1]))
  if (is.na(label) || !nzchar(label)) {
    v2_unnamed <- v2_unnamed + 1L
    label <- paste0("unnamed-chunk-", v2_unnamed)
  }
  v2_labels[i] <- label
  code <- code[!grepl("^\\s*#\\|", code)]
  v2_previous <- digest::digest(list(v2_previous, parse(text = code, keep.source = FALSE)))
  v2_code_keys[i] <- v2_previous
}
names(v2_code_keys) <- v2_labels
knitr::opts_hooks$set(cache = function(options) {
  if (isTRUE(options$cache)) {
    key <- v2_code_keys[options$label]
    if (length(key) != 1L || is.na(key)) stop("No cache dependency key for ", options$label)
    options$cache.extra <- list(v2_signature, unname(key))
  }
  options
})


v2_fit <- function(expr) {
  call <- substitute(expr)
  env <- parent.frame()
  data <- eval(call$data, envir = env)
  key <- digest::digest(list(call = paste(deparse(call), collapse = "\n"),
                            data = data, signature = v2_signature))
  path <- file.path(v2_dir, "models", paste0(as.character(call[[1]]), "-", key, ".rds"))
  if (file.exists(path)) return(readRDS(path))
  fit <- eval(call, envir = env)
  tmp <- tempfile(tmpdir = dirname(path))
  saveRDS(fit, tmp)
  if (!file.rename(tmp, path)) stop("Could not save model cache: ", path)
  fit
}

      )

# Reading and rebuilding this report {.unnumbered}

Recompile with `quarto render results.qmd --to html`. The first run fits models and obtains the World Bank GDP snapshot; later runs reuse results in `results_cache/`. Set `refresh_worldbank_gdp <- TRUE` in the setup chunk to update that snapshot.

# Results

## Data Processing and Exclusions


Exclusion criteria applied as stated in the [preregistration](https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/wegc5_v1):

> We will exclude participants who did not complete the study, failed an attention check question, failed to pass the Captcha test (i.e., their Captcha score is equal to or lower than 0.5), or are not permanent residents of the geopolitical region where data collection is taking place.

The exclusion counts are sequential: each row gives the additional participants removed after the preceding criteria. CAPTCHA scores equal to 0.5 are excluded, so the retained sample requires a score strictly above 0.5. The initial sample size, before any exclusions, was `r nrow(d)`.

```{r v2-chunk-003, echo=FALSE}
total_initial <- nrow(d)

excluded_finished <- total_initial  - nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1))
remaining_after_finished <- nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1))

excluded_recaptcha <- remaining_after_finished - nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1, 
                                                                   Q_RecaptchaScore > 0.5))
remaining_after_recaptcha <- nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1, 
                                               Q_RecaptchaScore > 0.5))

excluded_attcheck <- remaining_after_recaptcha - nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1, 
                                                                   Q_RecaptchaScore > 0.5,
                                                                   check==0))
remaining_after_attcheck <- nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1, 
                                               Q_RecaptchaScore > 0.5,
                                               check==0))

excluded_residence <- remaining_after_attcheck - nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1, 
                                                                   Q_RecaptchaScore > 0.5,
                                                                   check==0,
                                                                   Country_Res_YN =="Yes"))
remaining_after_residence <- nrow(d %>% filter(Finished == 1, 
                                               Q_RecaptchaScore > 0.5,
                                               check==0,
                                               Country_Res_YN =="Yes"))

excluded_country <- remaining_after_residence - nrow(d %>% filter(
  Finished == 1,
  Q_RecaptchaScore > 0.5,
  check == 0,
  Country_Res_YN == "Yes",
  !is.na(Country)
))

remaining_after_country <- remaining_after_residence - excluded_country

total_excluded <- total_initial - remaining_after_country

summary_table <- data.frame(
  Criterion = c(
    "Finished == 1",
    "Q_RecaptchaScore > 0.5",
    "attention check == 0",
    "Country_Res_YN == Yes",
    "`Country` not missing",
    "Total"
  ),
  Excluded = c(
    excluded_finished,
    excluded_recaptcha,
    excluded_attcheck,
    excluded_residence,
    excluded_country,
    total_excluded
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    Fraction = Excluded / total_initial,
    Percentage = Fraction * 100
  )

kable(
  summary_table,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  digits = c(0, 0, 3, 1),
  col.names = c(
    "Exclusion Criterion",
    "Number Excluded",
    "Fraction Excluded",
    "Percentage Excluded"
  ),
  caption = "Each line indicates how many participants failed each criterion (applied sequentially)."
)

```


```{r apply_exclusions, include=FALSE}
d <- d %>%
  filter(Finished == 1,
         check == 0,
         Q_RecaptchaScore > 0.5,
         Country_Res_YN =="Yes")

d <- d %>%
  filter(!is.na(Country))
```

## Demographic information

```{r v2-chunk-006, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
demographic_summary <- d %>%
  summarise(
    `Avearge age (Std.)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(Age, na.rm = TRUE), sd(Age, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `Age Range` = paste(min(Age, na.rm = TRUE), "to", max(Age, na.rm = TRUE)),
    `N. males` = sprintf("%i", sum(Gender == "Man", na.rm = TRUE)),
    `N. female` = sprintf("%i", sum(Gender == "Woman", na.rm = TRUE)),
    `N. non binary` = sprintf("%i", sum(Gender == "Non-binary", na.rm = TRUE)),
    `N. prefer not to respond` = sprintf("%i", sum(Gender ==  "Prefer not to respond", na.rm = TRUE)),
    `N. prefer to self-describe` = sprintf("%i", sum(Gender == "Prefer to self-describe", na.rm = TRUE))
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Demographic", values_to = "Value") 

knitr::kable(demographic_summary, booktabs = TRUE, 
             caption = "Demographic Information of Participants", 
             col.names = c("Demographic", "Value"))
```

The first demographic table summarizes age and reported gender in the retained sample. The next table separates those characteristics by the study’s country-level cultural classification.

```{r v2-chunk-007, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
demographic_summary <- d %>%
  filter(!is.na(culture)) %>%
  group_by(culture) %>%
  summarise(
    `N participants` = sprintf("%i", n()),
    `Average age (SD)` = sprintf(
      "%.2f (%.2f)",
      mean(Age, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd(Age, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    `Age range` = sprintf(
      "%g to %g",
      min(Age, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(Age, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    `N males` = sprintf("%i", sum(Gender == "Man", na.rm = TRUE)),
    `N females` = sprintf("%i", sum(Gender == "Woman", na.rm = TRUE)),
    `N non-binary` = sprintf("%i", sum(Gender == "Non-binary", na.rm = TRUE)),
    `N prefer not to respond` = sprintf(
      "%i",
      sum(Gender == "Prefer not to respond", na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    `N prefer to self-describe` = sprintf(
      "%i",
      sum(Gender == "Prefer to self-describe", na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -culture,
    names_to = "Demographic",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = culture,
    values_from = Value
  ) %>%
  select(
    Demographic,
    Individualistic,
    Collectivistic
  )

knitr::kable(
  demographic_summary,
  booktabs = TRUE,
  caption = "Demographic Information of Participants by Cultural Classification",
  col.names = c(
    "Demographic",
    "Individualistic",
    "Collectivistic"))

Education is reported as counts and percentages within each cultural group, so the columns can be compared despite different group sizes.

```{r v2-chunk-008}
#| echo: FALSE

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

education_table <- d %>%
  filter(!is.na(Edu), !is.na(culture)) %>%
  mutate(
    Edu = factor(
      Edu,
      levels = c(
        "Less than a high school or secondary school degree (or equivalent)",
        "High school or secondary school degree (or equivalent)",
        "Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent)",
        "Postgraduate degree (MA, PhD, JD, etc.)",
        "Prefer not to respond"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  count(culture, Edu, name = "N") %>%
  complete(culture, Edu, fill = list(N = 0)) %>%
  group_by(culture) %>%
  mutate(
    percent = 100 * N / sum(N),
    `N (%)` = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", format(N, big.mark = ","), percent)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(Education = Edu, culture, `N (%)`) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = culture,
    values_from = `N (%)`
  )

education_table %>%
  knitr::kable(
    align = c("l", "c", "c"),
    col.names = c(
      "Education level",
      "Collectivistic, N (%)",
      "Individualistic, N (%)"
    ),
    caption = "Level of education by cultural group."
  )
```


### Language background

Language fluency is summarized only among participants who said the study language was not their native language; the native-language rows use all participants who answered that question.
```{r v2-chunk-011, echo=FALSE}
library(gt)

d_lang <- d %>%
  mutate(
    lang_fluency_clean = case_when(
      str_detect(lang_fluency, "^Beginner") ~ "Beginner",
      str_detect(lang_fluency, "^Intermediate") ~ "Intermediate",
      str_detect(lang_fluency, "^Advanced") ~ "Advanced",
      str_detect(lang_fluency, "^Expert/Proficient") ~ "Expert/Proficient",
      lang_fluency == "Prefer not to respond" ~ "Prefer not to respond",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

native_summary <- d_lang %>%
  filter(!is.na(native_lang)) %>%
  count(response = native_lang) %>%
  mutate(
    section = "Native speaker of the study language",
    denominator = sum(n),
    percent = 100 * n / denominator
  )

fluency_summary <- d_lang %>%
  filter(
    native_lang == "No",
    !is.na(lang_fluency_clean)
  ) %>%
  count(response = lang_fluency_clean) %>%
  mutate(
    section = "Fluency among non-native speakers",
    denominator = sum(n),
    percent = 100 * n / denominator
  )

language_table <- bind_rows(
  native_summary,
  fluency_summary
) %>%
  mutate(
    response = factor(
      response,
      levels = c(
        "Yes", "No", "Prefer not to respond",
        "Beginner", "Intermediate", "Advanced",
        "Expert/Proficient"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(section, response) %>%
  select(section, response, n, percent)

language_table %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "section") %>%
  cols_label(
    response = "Response",
    n = "N",
    percent = "%"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = percent,

## Descriptive Statistics

### Use of external resources

This table describes how often participants reported outside-resource use for each problem and experimental condition. These responses inform the exclusions applied to the correction and confidence analyses.

```{r v2-chunk-009, echo=FALSE}
d %>%
  mutate(
    participant = row_number(),
    condition = case_when(
      feedback == "F"  & justification == "NJ" ~ "Feedback",
      feedback == "NF" & justification == "J"  ~ "Justification",
      feedback == "F"  & justification == "J"  ~ "Feedback + justification",
      .default = "Baseline"
    ),
    condition = factor(
      condition,
      levels = c(
        "Baseline",
        "Feedback",
        "Justification",
        "Feedback + justification"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    participant,
    condition,
    matches("^ext_resources_use_[1-6]$")
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^ext_resources_use_[1-6]$"),
    names_to = "problem",
    names_pattern = "ext_resources_use_(\\d+)",
    values_to = "ext_resources",
    values_drop_na = TRUE
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    problem = factor(
      paste("Problem", problem),
      levels = paste("Problem", 1:6)
    ),
    ext_resources = case_when(
      ext_resources == "Yes" ~ 1,
      ext_resources == "No"  ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(problem, condition) %>%
  summarise(
    percent = 100 * mean(ext_resources, na.rm = TRUE),
    N = sum(ext_resources, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    result = sprintf("%.2f%% (N = %d)", percent, N)
  ) %>%
  select(problem, condition, result) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = condition,
    values_from = result
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = c("l", "c", "c", "c", "c"),
    caption = paste(
      "Percentage and number of responses reporting use of external",
      "resources, split by problem and condition."
    )
  ) #%>%

```

### Familiarity

The table reports prior familiarity by problem and condition. Familiarity is descriptive here; the correction analyses exclude trials according to the analysis-specific rules shown in their methods.

```{r v2-chunk-010, echo=FALSE}

### Pooled response pattern counts (H2/H3 exclusion criteria)

```{r dadd-chunk-002, echo=FALSE}
d_desc <- d_all %>%
  filter(ext_resources_use=="No")  %>%
  mutate(
    Condition = case_when(
      feedback == "NF" & justification == "NJ" ~ "Control",
      feedback == "F"  & justification == "NJ" ~ "Feedback",
      feedback == "NF" & justification == "J"  ~ "Justification",
      feedback == "F"  & justification == "J"  ~ "Feedback + justification"
    )
  )

summarise_patterns <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    summarise(
      N = n(),
      `Correct → Correct` = sum(accuracy_intuitive == 1 & accuracy_reflective == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
      `Correct → Incorrect` = sum(accuracy_intuitive == 1 & accuracy_reflective == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      `Incorrect → Correct` = sum(accuracy_intuitive == 0 & accuracy_reflective == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
      `Incorrect → Incorrect` = sum(accuracy_intuitive == 0 & accuracy_reflective == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      Missing = sum(is.na(accuracy_intuitive) | is.na(accuracy_reflective)),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      `% correct via correction` = round(
        100 * `Incorrect → Correct` /
          (`Correct → Correct` + `Incorrect → Correct`), 1
      )
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      across(
        c(`Correct → Correct`, `Correct → Incorrect`,
          `Incorrect → Correct`, `Incorrect → Incorrect`, Missing),
        ~ sprintf("%.0f (%.1f%%)", .x,
                  if_else(N > 0, 100 * .x / N, NA_real_))
      )
    )
}

h23_descriptives <- bind_rows(
  d_desc %>%
    group_by(Condition) %>%
    summarise_patterns(),
  
  d_desc %>%
    summarise_patterns() %>%
    mutate(Condition = "Overall")
)

knitr::kable(h23_descriptives, digits = 1)

The table below gives accuracy by problem and experimental condition in the analytic sample used for H1. It provides a descriptive view of performance before the country-level mixed models.

```{r v2-chunk-013, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

  filter(!is.na(accuracy_intuitive))  %>%
  group_by(justification, feedback, problem) %>%

            reflective = mean(accuracy_reflective))

knitr::kable(mean_accuracy_table,
             booktabs = TRUE, 
             caption = "Mean accuracy by CRT problem and phase (here 'intuitive' is phase 1 and 'reflective' is phase 2). Computed after applying exclusion criteria based on on familiarity and use of external resource.",
             digits=2) # %>%
```

Figure @fig-pH1 summarizes the H1 outcome in the no-feedback, no-justification condition. Country points are based on participant-level correction proportions, with uncertainty shown across participants.

```{r models_H1, include=FALSE}
mH1_all <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ feedback * justification + 
   (feedback * justification||Country), 
   family = binomial("logit"), data = dat_H1, 
   control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", 
      optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))

mH1_i <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ feedback * justification + 
   (feedback * justification||Country), 
   family = binomial("logit"), 
   data = dat_H1[dat_H1$culture == "Individualistic", ], 
   control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", 
     optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))

mH1_c <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ feedback * justification + 
   (feedback * justification||Country), 
   family = binomial("logit"), 
   data = dat_H1[dat_H1$culture == "Collectivistic", ], 
   control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", 
      optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))

alpha <- 0.05
 
 
b_H1a <- fixef(mH1_all)["(Intercept)"]
SE_H1a <- sqrt(diag(vcov(mH1_all))["(Intercept)"])
z_H1a <- b_H1a / SE_H1a
p_value_H1a <- pnorm(z_H1a) # left-tailed test
H1a <- ifelse(p_value_H1a < alpha, 1, 0)
 
models <- list(mH1_i, mH1_c)
names <- c("Individualistic", "Collectivistic")
H1b_pvals <- numeric(length(models))
H1b_results <- numeric(length(models))
z_H1b <- numeric(length(models))
 
for (i in 1:length(models)) {
  b <- fixef(models[[i]])["(Intercept)"]
  SE <- sqrt(diag(vcov(models[[i]]))["(Intercept)"])
  z <- b / SE
  p_value <- pnorm(z) # left-tailed test
  z_H1b[i] <- z
  H1b_pvals[i] <- p_value
  H1b_results[i] <- ifelse(p_value < alpha, 1, 0)
}

names(z_H1b) <- names
names(H1b_pvals) <- names
names(H1b_results) <- names

H1b <- ifelse(all(H1b_results == 1), 1, 0)

model_table <- function(model, caption = NULL, group = "Country",
                        term_labels = NULL, digits = 3) {

  tab_fixed <- broom.mixed::tidy(
    model,
    effects = "fixed",
    conf.int = TRUE
  )

  if (!is.null(term_labels)) {
    ii <- match(tab_fixed$term, names(term_labels))
    tab_fixed$term[!is.na(ii)] <- term_labels[ii[!is.na(ii)]]
  }

  tab_fixed <- tab_fixed %>%
    transmute(
      Predictor = term,
      Estimate = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), estimate),
      SE = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), std.error),
      `95% CI` = sprintf(
        paste0("[%.", digits, "f, %.", digits, "f]"),
        conf.low, conf.high
      ),
      `p-value` = case_when(
        p.value < .001 ~ "< .001",
        TRUE ~ sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))
      )
    )

  vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(model)) %>%
    filter(is.na(var2))  # retain SDs, not correlations

  vc$grp <- sub("\\.[0-9]+$", "", vc$grp)

  if (!is.null(term_labels)) {
    ii <- match(vc$var1, names(term_labels))
    vc$var1[!is.na(ii)] <- term_labels[ii[!is.na(ii)]]
  }

  tab_random <- vc %>%
    filter(grp != "Residual") %>%
    transmute(
      Predictor = paste0("SD (", grp, ": ", var1, ")"),
      Estimate = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), sdcor),
      SE = "",
      `95% CI` = "",
      `p-value` = ""
    )

  n <- nobs(model)

  n_groups <- if (group %in% names(model.frame(model))) {
    dplyr::n_distinct(model.frame(model)[[group]])
  } else {
    NA_integer_
  }

  tab_info <- tibble(
    Predictor = c("N", paste0("N ", group)),
    Estimate = c(as.character(n), as.character(n_groups)),
    SE = "",
    `95% CI` = "",
    `p-value` = ""
  )

  bind_rows(
    tab_fixed,
    tab_random,
    tab_info
  ) %>%
    knitr::kable(
      caption = caption,
      align = c("l", "r", "r", "c", "r")
    )
}

```

### Models for H1a and H1b (correction during deliberation)

```{r v2-chunk-016, include=FALSE}

   (feedback * justification||Country),

     optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))

m_i <- v2_fit(glmer(corrected ~ feedback * justification + 
   (feedback * justification||Country), 
  family = binomial("logit"), 
  data = dat_Hother[dat_Hother$culture == "Individualistic", ],

   (feedback * justification||Country), 
  family = binomial("logit"),

  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa",

alpha <- 0.05

 
 
b_H2a <- fixef(m_all)["feedback"]
SE_H2a <- sqrt(diag(vcov(m_all))["feedback"])
z_H2a <- b_H2a / SE_H2a
p_value_H2a <- 1 - pnorm(z_H2a) # right-tailed test
H2a <- ifelse(p_value_H2a < alpha, 1, 0)

for (i in 1:length(models)) {
  b <- fixef(models[[i]])["feedback"]
  SE <- sqrt(diag(vcov(models[[i]]))["feedback"])

  p_value <- 1 - pnorm(z) # right-tailed test
  z_H2b[i] <- z

}

```

The condition tables report model-estimated proportions from the fixed effects, with random effects set to zero. The 95% confidence intervals are pointwise Wald intervals calculated on the logit scale and transformed back to probabilities; they quantify uncertainty in the fixed-effect predictions, rather than variation across countries, problems, or sites. For H1, the outcome is first becoming correct in the reflective phase among trials correct in either phase. For H2/H3, it is correcting an initially incorrect response.

```{r condition-probability-helpers, include=FALSE}
model_condition_probabilities <- function(model) {
  # Explicitly retain both levels of the numeric 0/1 treatment predictors.
  # Use the fitted model frame so the estimates use this model's analysis sample.
  emm <- emmeans::emmeans(
    model, ~ feedback * justification,
    at = list(feedback = c(0, 1), justification = c(0, 1)),
    data = model.frame(model), df = Inf
  )
  as.data.frame(confint(emm, level = 0.95, type = "response", adjust = "none")) %>%
    arrange(justification, feedback) %>%
    transmute(
      Condition = case_when(
        feedback == 0 & justification == 0 ~ "Control",
        feedback == 1 & justification == 0 ~ "Feedback only",
        feedback == 0 & justification == 1 ~ "Justification only",
        feedback == 1 & justification == 1 ~ "Feedback and justification"
      ),
      estimate = prob,
      lower = asymp.LCL,
      upper = asymp.UCL
    )
}

model_probability_table <- function(model, caption) {
  model_condition_probabilities(model) %>%
    transmute(
      Condition,
      `Estimated proportion` = sprintf("%.2f", estimate),
      `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", lower, upper)
    ) %>%
    knitr::kable(booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", "r", "c"), caption = caption)
}
```

The H1 models estimate the preregistered probability outcomes with country-varying manipulation effects. The hypothesis summary combines the overall test with the requirement that the directional result also appear in both cultural groups.

The models test feedback and justification effects on the probability of correcting an initially incorrect intuitive response in the reflective phase. The coefficient tables report the overall estimates and then the country-group estimates; the hypothesis summary below translates the preregistered one-tailed tests into supported/not-supported outcomes.

```{r}
#| fig-align: 'center'
#| echo: FALSE
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Probability of correcting an intuitive-phase error in the reflective phase (the outcome in H2 and H3), by country and culture, shown separately for each feedback and justification condition. Each country point is the mean of participant-level correction proportions; error bars show bootstrap standard errors across participants within country and condition."
#| label: fig-pH2H3

dat_Hother %>%
  group_by(Country, culture, feedback, justification, participant) %>%
  summarise(corrected = mean(corrected), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Country, culture, feedback, justification) %>%
  summarise(se = mlisi::bootMeanSE(corrected),
            y = mean(corrected),
            n_participants = n(),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    culture = factor(culture, levels = c("Collectivistic", "Individualistic")),
    feedback_condition = factor(feedback, levels = c(0, 1),
                                labels = c("No feedback", "Feedback")),
    justification_condition = factor(justification, levels = c(0, 1),
                                     labels = c("No justification", "Justification"))
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = culture, y = y, color = culture)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se),
                width = 0, color = "dark grey",
                position = position_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, seed = 20261016)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, seed = 20261016)) +
  facet_grid(justification_condition ~ feedback_condition) +
  ml_theme() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.2)) +
  labs(y = "Probability of correcting an intuitive-phase error", x = "") +
  scale_color_discrete(guide = "none")
```

### Confirmatory hypothesis testing summary

```{r v2-chunk-021, echo=FALSE}
format_p <- function(p, digits = 3) {
  case_when(
    is.na(p)  ~ NA_character_,
    p < 0.001 ~ "< .001",
    TRUE      ~ sub("^0", "", sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), p))
  )
}

format_z <- function(z, digits = 2) {
  case_when(
    is.na(z)  ~ NA_character_,
    TRUE      ~ sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), z)
  )
}

format_culture_p <- function(p) {
  paste0(
    names(p),
    " = ",
    format_p(unname(p)),
    collapse = "; "
  )
}

format_culture_z <- function(z) {
  paste0(
    names(z),
    " = ",
    format_z(unname(z)),
    collapse = "; "
  )
}

H1a_supported <- H1a == 1
H1b_supported <- all(H1b_results == 1)

H2a_supported <- H2a == 1
H2b_supported <- all(H2b_results == 1)

H3a_supported <- H3a == 1
H3b_supported <- all(H3b_results == 1)

hypothesis_results <- tribble(
  ~Hypothesis, ~Prediction, ~Supported, ~`Wald Z`, ~`p-value(s)`,

  "H1a",
  "Less than half of correct answers will arise from error correction during deliberation",
  H1a_supported,
  format_z(z_H1a),
  format_p(p_value_H1a),

  "H1b",
  "Baseline performance is below 50% in both cultural groups",
  H1b_supported,
  format_culture_z(z_H1b),
  format_culture_p(H1b_pvals),

  "H2a",
  "Feedback increases correction overall",
  H2a_supported,
  format_z(z_H2a),
  format_p(p_value_H2a),

  "H2b",
  "Feedback increases correction in both cultural groups",
  H2b_supported,
  format_culture_z(z_H2b),
  format_culture_p(H2b_pvals),

  "H3a",
  "Justification increases correction overall",
  H3a_supported,
  format_z(z_H3a),
  format_p(p_value_H3a),

  "H3b",
  "Justification increases correction in both cultural groups",
  H3b_supported,
  format_culture_z(z_H3b),
  format_culture_p(H3b_pvals)
) %>%
  mutate(
    Supported = case_when(
      is.na(Supported) ~ "Not estimable",
      Supported        ~ "Yes",
      TRUE             ~ "No"
    )
  )

hypothesis_results %>%
  kable(
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = c("l", "l", "c", "l"),
    caption = paste(
      "Summary of preregistered hypothesis tests after including",
      "by-problem random intercepts"
    )
  ) # %>%
```

The summary records the preregistered one-tailed tests at α = .05. A hypothesis is marked supported only when its stated overall or group-specific criteria are met; the table retains the p-values used for that decision.

## Robustness Checks

### Random Effects for CRT Problem

These models add a random intercept for CRT problem to account for differences in baseline problem difficulty. The fixed-effect hypotheses and country random slopes otherwise follow the confirmatory models.

```{r models_H1_check1, include=FALSE}
mH1_all <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ feedback * justification + 
   (feedback * justification||Country)+ (1|problem), 
   family = binomial("logit"), data = dat_H1, 
   control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", 
      optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))

mH1_i <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ feedback * justification + 
   (feedback * justification||Country)+ (1|problem), 
   family = binomial("logit"), 
   data = dat_H1[dat_H1$culture == "Individualistic", ], 
   control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", 
     optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))

mH1_c <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ feedback * justification + 
   (feedback * justification||Country)+ (1|problem), 
   family = binomial("logit"), 
   data = dat_H1[dat_H1$culture == "Collectivistic", ], 
   control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", 
      optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))

alpha <- 0.05
 
 
b_H1a <- fixef(mH1_all)["(Intercept)"]
SE_H1a <- sqrt(diag(vcov(mH1_all))["(Intercept)"])
z_H1a <- b_H1a / SE_H1a
p_value_H1a <- pnorm(z_H1a) # left-tailed test
H1a <- ifelse(p_value_H1a < alpha, 1, 0)
 
models <- list(mH1_i, mH1_c)
names <- c("Individualistic", "Collectivistic")
H1b_pvals <- numeric(length(models))
H1b_results <- numeric(length(models))
z_H1b <- numeric(length(models))
 
for (i in 1:length(models)) {
  b <- fixef(models[[i]])["(Intercept)"]
  SE <- sqrt(diag(vcov(models[[i]]))["(Intercept)"])
  z <- b / SE
  p_value <- pnorm(z) # left-tailed test
  z_H1b[i] <- z
  H1b_pvals[i] <- p_value
  H1b_results[i] <- ifelse(p_value < alpha, 1, 0)
}

names(z_H1b) <- names
names(H1b_pvals) <- names
names(H1b_results) <- names

H1b <- ifelse(all(H1b_results == 1), 1, 0)

model_table_2 <- function(model, caption = NULL,
                        term_labels = NULL, digits = 3) {

  tab_fixed <- broom.mixed::tidy(
    model,
    effects = "fixed",
    conf.int = TRUE
  )

  if (!is.null(term_labels)) {
    ii <- match(tab_fixed$term, names(term_labels))
    tab_fixed$term[!is.na(ii)] <- term_labels[ii[!is.na(ii)]]
  }

  tab_fixed <- tab_fixed %>%
    transmute(
      Predictor = term,
      Estimate = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), estimate),
      SE = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), std.error),
      `95% CI` = sprintf(
        paste0("[%.", digits, "f, %.", digits, "f]"),
        conf.low, conf.high
      ),
      `p-value` = case_when(
        p.value < .001 ~ "< .001",
        TRUE ~ sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))
      )
    )

  vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(model)) %>%
    filter(is.na(var2))  # variance/SD terms only

  vc$grp <- sub("\\.[0-9]+$", "", vc$grp)

  if (!is.null(term_labels)) {
    ii <- match(vc$var1, names(term_labels))
    vc$var1[!is.na(ii)] <- term_labels[ii[!is.na(ii)]]
  }

  tab_random <- vc %>%
    filter(grp != "Residual") %>%
    transmute(
      Predictor = paste0("SD (", grp, ": ", var1, ")"),
      Estimate = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), sdcor),
      SE = "",
      `95% CI` = "",
      `p-value` = ""
    )

  n <- nobs(model)

  ng <- lme4::ngrps(model)

  tab_info <- tibble(
    Predictor = c(
      "N",
      paste0("N ", names(ng))
    ),
    Estimate = c(
      as.character(n),
      as.character(ng)
    ),
    SE = "",
    `95% CI` = "",
    `p-value` = ""
  )

  bind_rows(
    tab_fixed,
    tab_random,
    tab_info
  ) %>%
    knitr::kable(
      caption = caption,
      align = c("l", "r", "r", "c", "r")
    )
}

  format_culture_p(H2b_pvals),

  "H3a",
  "Justification increases correction overall",
  H3a_supported,
  format_z(z_H3a),
  format_p(p_value_H3a),

  "H3b",
  "Justification increases correction in both cultural groups",
  H3b_supported,
  format_culture_z(z_H3b),
  format_culture_p(H3b_pvals)
) %>%
  mutate(
    Supported = case_when(
      is.na(Supported) ~ "Not estimable",
      Supported        ~ "Yes",
      TRUE             ~ "No"
    )
  )

hypothesis_results %>%
  kable(
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = c("l", "l", "c", "l", "l"),
    caption = paste(
      "Summary of preregistered hypothesis tests after including",
      "by-problem random intercepts"
    )
  ) # %>%
```

Compare these results with the primary hypothesis summary: changes indicate how sensitive the conclusions are to allowing baseline accuracy to vary across CRT problems.


### Random Effects for Participating Site

This robustness set adds a lab/site random intercept, accounting for clustering within participating sites while retaining country-level treatment slopes.


```{r models_H1_check2, include=FALSE}
mH1_all <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ feedback * justification + 
   (feedback * justification||Country)+ (1|LabID), 
   family = binomial("logit"), data = dat_H1, 
   control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", 
      optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))

mH1_i <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ feedback * justification + 
   (feedback * justification||Country)+ (1|LabID), 
   family = binomial("logit"), 
   data = dat_H1[dat_H1$culture == "Individualistic", ], 
   control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", 
     optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))

mH1_c <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ feedback * justification + 
   (feedback * justification||Country)+ (1|LabID), 
   family = binomial("logit"), 
   data = dat_H1[dat_H1$culture == "Collectivistic", ], 
   control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", 
      optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))

alpha <- 0.05
 
 
b_H1a <- fixef(mH1_all)["(Intercept)"]
SE_H1a <- sqrt(diag(vcov(mH1_all))["(Intercept)"])
z_H1a <- b_H1a / SE_H1a
p_value_H1a <- pnorm(z_H1a) # left-tailed test
H1a <- ifelse(p_value_H1a < alpha, 1, 0)
 
models <- list(mH1_i, mH1_c)
names <- c("Individualistic", "Collectivistic")
H1b_pvals <- numeric(length(models))
H1b_results <- numeric(length(models))
z_H1b <- numeric(length(models))
 
for (i in 1:length(models)) {
  b <- fixef(models[[i]])["(Intercept)"]
  SE <- sqrt(diag(vcov(models[[i]]))["(Intercept)"])
  z <- b / SE
  p_value <- pnorm(z) # left-tailed test
  z_H1b[i] <- z
  H1b_pvals[i] <- p_value
  H1b_results[i] <- ifelse(p_value < alpha, 1, 0)
}

names(z_H1b) <- names
names(H1b_pvals) <- names
names(H1b_results) <- names

H1b <- ifelse(all(H1b_results == 1), 1, 0)

```

#### Hypothesis testing summary

```{r v2-chunk-035, echo=FALSE}
format_p <- function(p, digits = 3) {
  case_when(
    is.na(p)  ~ NA_character_,
    p < 0.001 ~ "< .001",
    TRUE      ~ sub("^0", "", sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), p))
  )
}

format_culture_p <- function(p) {
  paste0(
    names(p),
    " = ",
    format_p(unname(p)),
    collapse = "; "
  )
}

format_z <- function(z, digits = 2) {
  case_when(
    is.na(z)  ~ NA_character_,
    TRUE      ~ sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), z)
  )
}

format_culture_z <- function(z) {
  paste0(
    names(z),
    " = ",
    format_z(unname(z)),
    collapse = "; "
  )
}

## Exploratory Analyses

### Continuous global collectivism (exploratory)

These models use the country-level Global Collectivism Index (GCI; named `CGI` in the dataset) on its original continuous scale, replacing the binary cultural grouping. Both outcomes include the feedback × justification × GCI interaction and a problem random intercept; country-level random effects retain the specifications in `scrap_continuous_models.R`. Companion models add standardized log GDP per capita as an additive country-level covariate. The GDP adjustment asks whether the GCI associations persist after accounting for national income; it does not estimate a GDP interaction. GCI = 0 is the reference for manipulation coefficients; the three-way term tests whether the feedback-by-justification interaction changes with GCI.

```{r continuous-gci-data}
gci_H1 <- dat_H1 %>% filter(is.finite(CGI), !is.na(correct_phase2))
gci_correction <- dat_Hother %>% filter(is.finite(CGI), !is.na(corrected))
gci_samples <- bind_rows(
  summarise(gci_H1, Outcome = "H1", Trials = n(), Participants = n_distinct(participant),
            Countries = n_distinct(Country), Minimum = min(CGI), Maximum = max(CGI)),
  summarise(gci_correction, Outcome = "Correction", Trials = n(), Participants = n_distinct(participant),
            Countries = n_distinct(Country), Minimum = min(CGI), Maximum = max(CGI)))
knitr::kable(gci_samples, digits = 2, caption = "Complete-case samples and observed GCI ranges.")

gci_countries <- union(unique(gci_H1$Country), unique(gci_correction$Country))
gdp_scale <- country_gdp_lookup %>%
  filter(Country %in% gci_countries, is.finite(GDP_per_capita_current_USD),
         GDP_per_capita_current_USD > 0) %>%
  distinct(Country, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  summarise(mean_log_GDP = mean(log(GDP_per_capita_current_USD)),
            sd_log_GDP = sd(log(GDP_per_capita_current_USD)))

gci_H1_gdp <- gci_H1 %>%
  filter(is.finite(GDP_per_capita_current_USD), GDP_per_capita_current_USD > 0) %>%
  mutate(log_GDP_pc_z = (log(GDP_per_capita_current_USD) - gdp_scale$mean_log_GDP) /
           gdp_scale$sd_log_GDP)

gci_correction_gdp <- gci_correction %>%
  filter(is.finite(GDP_per_capita_current_USD), GDP_per_capita_current_USD > 0) %>%
  mutate(log_GDP_pc_z = (log(GDP_per_capita_current_USD) - gdp_scale$mean_log_GDP) /
           gdp_scale$sd_log_GDP)

gci_gdp_samples <- bind_rows(
  summarise(gci_H1_gdp, Outcome = "H1", Trials = n(),
            Participants = n_distinct(participant), Countries = n_distinct(Country)),
  summarise(gci_correction_gdp, Outcome = "Correction", Trials = n(),
            Participants = n_distinct(participant), Countries = n_distinct(Country))
)
knitr::kable(gci_gdp_samples,
             caption = "Complete-case samples for the GDP-adjusted models.")

gdp_coverage <- country_gdp_lookup %>%
  filter(Country %in% gci_countries) %>%
  arrange(Country) %>%
  select(Country, GDP_year, GDP_per_capita_current_USD)
knitr::kable(gdp_coverage, digits = 0,
             caption = "World Bank GDP per-capita observation used for each country with GCI data. Missing values are excluded from the GDP-adjusted models.")
knitr::kable(wb_provenance,
             caption = "World Bank source and retrieval details for the cached GDP snapshot.")
```

GDP per capita is the World Bank’s `NY.GDP.PCAP.CD` series in current US dollars. The API query selects each country’s latest non-missing observation; the year and value are listed above, and the exact downloaded snapshot is kept in `results_cache/data/`. See the World Bank’s [Indicators API documentation](https://datahelpdesk.worldbank.org/knowledgebase/articles/898599-indicator-api-queries). Because countries’ latest observation years can differ, this is a sensitivity covariate rather than a synchronized study-year measure. The GDP-adjusted models use the standardized natural log of GDP per capita, with scaling based on one record per country.

```{r continuous-gci-models}
mH1_all_cgi <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ feedback * justification * CGI +
  (feedback + feedback:justification || Country) + (1 | problem),
  family = binomial("logit"), data = gci_H1,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))
m_all_cgi <- v2_fit(glmer(corrected ~ feedback * justification * CGI +
  (feedback * justification || Country) + (1 | problem),
  family = binomial("logit"), data = gci_correction,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))
 mH1_all_cgi_gdp <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ feedback * justification * CGI + log_GDP_pc_z +
  (feedback + feedback:justification || Country) + (1 | problem),
  family = binomial("logit"), data = gci_H1_gdp,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))
m_all_cgi_gdp <- v2_fit(glmer(corrected ~ feedback * justification * CGI + log_GDP_pc_z +
  (feedback * justification || Country) + (1 | problem),
  family = binomial("logit"), data = gci_correction_gdp,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))
model_table_2(mH1_all_cgi, caption = "Continuous GCI: correction during deliberation (H1 outcome).")
model_table_2(m_all_cgi, caption = "Continuous GCI: correction of initially incorrect responses.")
model_table_2(mH1_all_cgi_gdp, caption = "Continuous GCI plus GDP per capita: correction during deliberation (H1 outcome).")
model_table_2(m_all_cgi_gdp, caption = "Continuous GCI plus GDP per capita: correction of initially incorrect responses.")
```

For each outcome, the first coefficient table estimates the association with GCI alone; the companion table estimates that association conditional on standardized log GDP per capita. Interpret the GDP coefficient as an adjusted country-level association and the GCI-by-treatment terms as moderation of the experimental effects.

```{r continuous-gci-diagnostics}
v2_glmer_diagnostics <- function(model, label) {
  msg <- model@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages
  tibble(Model = label, Trials = nobs(model), Singular = isSingular(model),
         Optimizer_code = paste(model@optinfo$conv$opt, collapse = "; "),
         Convergence = if (is.null(msg)) "No lme4 convergence messages" else paste(msg, collapse = "; "))
}
knitr::kable(bind_rows(v2_glmer_diagnostics(mH1_all_cgi, "H1"),
                      v2_glmer_diagnostics(m_all_cgi, "Correction"),
                      v2_glmer_diagnostics(mH1_all_cgi_gdp, "H1 + GDP"),
                      v2_glmer_diagnostics(m_all_cgi_gdp, "Correction + GDP")),
             caption = "Continuous-GCI model diagnostics; inspect warnings before interpretation.")
```

The diagnostics show sample size, singularity, and optimizer messages for each fit. Singular or non-converged models need cautious interpretation even if a coefficient table is available.

```{r continuous-gci-predictions}
v2_gci_predictions <- function(model, data, label) {
  nd <- expand_grid(CGI = seq(min(data$CGI), max(data$CGI), length.out = 100),
                    feedback = 0:1, justification = 0:1)
  X <- model.matrix(~ feedback * justification * CGI, nd)
  X <- X[, names(fixef(model)), drop = FALSE]
  eta <- as.numeric(X %*% fixef(model))
  se <- sqrt(pmax(0, rowSums((X %*% as.matrix(vcov(model))) * X)))
  nd %>% mutate(fit = plogis(eta), lower = plogis(eta - 1.96 * se),
                upper = plogis(eta + 1.96 * se), Outcome = label,
                Feedback = factor(feedback, 0:1, c("No feedback", "Feedback")),
                Justification = factor(justification, 0:1, c("No justification", "Justification")))
}
pred_gci <- bind_rows(v2_gci_predictions(mH1_all_cgi, gci_H1, "H1 outcome"),
                      v2_gci_predictions(m_all_cgi, gci_correction, "Correction"))
v2_gci_predictions_gdp <- function(model, data, label) {
  nd <- expand_grid(CGI = seq(min(data$CGI), max(data$CGI), length.out = 100),
                    feedback = 0:1, justification = 0:1) %>%
    mutate(log_GDP_pc_z = 0)
  X <- model.matrix(~ feedback * justification * CGI + log_GDP_pc_z, nd)
  X <- X[, names(fixef(model)), drop = FALSE]
  eta <- as.numeric(X %*% fixef(model))
  se <- sqrt(pmax(0, rowSums((X %*% as.matrix(vcov(model))) * X)))
  nd %>% mutate(fit = plogis(eta), lower = plogis(eta - 1.96 * se),
                upper = plogis(eta + 1.96 * se), Outcome = label,
                Feedback = factor(feedback, 0:1, c("No feedback", "Feedback")),
                Justification = factor(justification, 0:1,
                                       c("No justification", "Justification")))
}
pred_gci_gdp <- bind_rows(
  v2_gci_predictions_gdp(mH1_all_cgi_gdp, gci_H1_gdp, "H1 outcome"),
  v2_gci_predictions_gdp(m_all_cgi_gdp, gci_correction_gdp, "Correction")
)
saveRDS(pred_gci, file.path(v2_dir, "derived", "continuous-gci-predictions.rds"))
saveRDS(pred_gci_gdp, file.path(v2_dir, "derived", "continuous-gci-gdp-predictions.rds"))
```

ggplot(pred_gci, aes(CGI, fit, colour = Feedback, fill = Feedback)) +

  geom_line() + facet_grid(Outcome ~ Justification) +

### Scales reliability and measurement invariance

All three measurement-invariance analyses are refitted on the sample surviving the preregistered exclusions and saved as fitted models in `results_cache/models/`. IH and AOT include countries with at least 100 participants; IC uses the 200-participant threshold. The alpha tables describe internal consistency, while the multi-group CFAs test whether the selected measurement parameters are comparable across countries.

#### Intellectual humility

```{r v2-chunk-041}

IH_alpha_country <- d %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    
    x <- .x[, IH_items]
    
    a <- tryCatch(
      psych::alpha(x, check.keys = FALSE, warnings = FALSE)$total$raw_alpha,
      error = function(e) NA_real_
    )
    
    tibble(
      N = nrow(.x),
      alpha = a
    )
    
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(N))

knitr::kable(
  IH_alpha_country[IH_alpha_country$N >= 100,],
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Internal consistency of the Intellectual Humility scale by country (only countries with N>100 shown)."
)
```

Country-level IH alpha values in the displayed sample range from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(IH_alpha_country$alpha[IH_alpha_country$N >= 100], na.rm = TRUE))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(IH_alpha_country$alpha[IH_alpha_country$N >= 100], na.rm = TRUE))`; alpha is a descriptive internal-consistency index, not evidence of measurement invariance.

```{r v2-chunk-042, echo=FALSE}


IH_model <- '
  IH =~ IH_1 + IH_2 + IH_3 + IH_4 + IH_5 +
        IH_6 + IH_7 + IH_8 + IH_9

  POS =~ IH_1 + IH_2 + IH_3 + IH_4 + IH_5 + IH_7
  NEG =~ IH_6 + IH_8 + IH_9

  IH ~~ 0*POS
  IH ~~ 0*NEG

  POS ~~ NEG
  POS ~~ 1*POS
  NEG ~~ 1*NEG'

country_N <- table(d$Country)
countries_MI <- names(country_N[country_N >= 100])
d_IH_MI <- d %>%
  filter(Country %in% countries_MI)

fit_IH_config <- v2_fit(cfa(
  IH_model,
  data = d_IH_MI,
  group = "Country",
  estimator = "MLR",
  std.lv = TRUE,
  missing = "listwise"
))

POS_items <- c("IH_1", "IH_2", "IH_3", "IH_4", "IH_5", "IH_7")
NEG_items <- c("IH_6", "IH_8", "IH_9")

method_loadings <- c(
  paste0("POS=~", POS_items),
  paste0("NEG=~", NEG_items))

fit_IH_metric <- v2_fit(cfa(
  IH_model,
  data = d_IH_MI,
  group = "Country",
  estimator = "MLR",
  std.lv = TRUE,
  missing = "listwise",
  group.equal = "loadings",
  group.partial = method_loadings # Do NOT constrain wording-factor loadings (see note above)
))

fit_IH_scalar <- v2_fit(cfa(
  IH_model,
  data = d_IH_MI,
  group = "Country",
  estimator = "MLR",
  std.lv = TRUE,
  missing =  "listwise",
  group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"),
  group.partial = method_loadings
))

get_MI_fit <- function(fit) {
  fitMeasures(
    fit,
    c("cfi.robust", "tli.robust", "rmsea.robust", "srmr")
  )
}

v2_cfa_diagnostics <- function(fit, label) {
  pt <- parameterTable(fit)
  tibble(
    Model = label,
    Participants = sum(lavInspect(fit, "nobs")),
    Countries = lavInspect(fit, "ngroups"),
    Converged = isTRUE(lavInspect(fit, "converged")),
    Admissible = isTRUE(tryCatch(lavInspect(fit, "post.check"),
                                 error = function(e) FALSE)),
    Finite_SE = all(is.finite(pt$se[pt$free > 0]))
  )
}

fits_IH <- rbind(
  Configural = get_MI_fit(fit_IH_config),
  Metric     = get_MI_fit(fit_IH_metric),
  Scalar     = get_MI_fit(fit_IH_scalar)
)

fits_IH <- cbind(
  fits_IH,
  delta_CFI = c(
    NA,
    fits_IH["Metric", "cfi.robust"] -
      fits_IH["Configural", "cfi.robust"],
    fits_IH["Scalar", "cfi.robust"] -
      fits_IH["Metric", "cfi.robust"]
  ),
  delta_RMSEA = c(
    NA,
    fits_IH["Metric", "rmsea.robust"] -
      fits_IH["Configural", "rmsea.robust"],
    fits_IH["Scalar", "rmsea.robust"] -
      fits_IH["Metric", "rmsea.robust"]
  ),
  delta_SRMR = c(
    NA,
    fits_IH["Metric", "srmr"] - fits_IH["Configural", "srmr"],
    fits_IH["Scalar", "srmr"] - fits_IH["Metric", "srmr"]
  )
)

saveRDS(
  list(
    fits_IH = fits_IH,
    fit_IH_config = fit_IH_config,
    fit_IH_metric = fit_IH_metric,
    fit_IH_scalar = fit_IH_scalar
  ),
  file = file.path(v2_dir, "derived", "IH_measurement_invariance.rds")
)

```

fits_IH <- IH_MI$fits_IH

IH_fit_table <- as.data.frame(fits_IH) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Model") %>%
  transmute(
    Model,
    CFI = cfi.robust,
    TLI = tli.robust,
    RMSEA = rmsea.robust,
    SRMR = srmr,
    `ΔCFI` = delta_CFI,
    `ΔRMSEA` = delta_RMSEA,
    `ΔSRMR` = delta_SRMR
  )

knitr::kable(
  IH_fit_table,

  caption = "Measurement invariance analysis for the Intellectual Humility scale",
  align = c("l", rep("c", 7))

  v2_cfa_diagnostics(IH_MI$fit_IH_metric, "Metric"),

```

The IH CFA separates substantive IH from positive- and negative-wording method factors. Method-factor loadings remain free between countries; their variances are fixed to one to identify their scale. The identified configural model has robust CFI `r sprintf("%.3f", fits_IH["Configural", "cfi.robust"])`. Metric and scalar ΔCFI are `r sprintf("%.3f", fits_IH["Metric", "cfi.robust"] - fits_IH["Configural", "cfi.robust"])` and `r sprintf("%.3f", fits_IH["Scalar", "cfi.robust"] - fits_IH["Metric", "cfi.robust"])`, respectively. Use the full fit table and diagnostics alongside the descriptive .01 ΔCFI reference when judging cross-country comparability.

#### Actively open-minded thinking scale


The table below uses the 13 AOT items after the reverse scoring already applied during data preparation. Raw Cronbach’s alpha is calculated using pairwise-complete item data, matching the IH reliability analysis; no automatic item reversal is applied. Countries with at least 100 participants are shown. Complete-item counts indicate how many participants answered every AOT item.

```{r aot-alpha-by-country}
AOT_alpha_country <- d %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
    items <- .x[, AOT_items]
    alpha <- tryCatch(
      psych::alpha(items, check.keys = FALSE, warnings = FALSE,
                   use = "pairwise")$total$raw_alpha,
      error = function(e) NA_real_
    )
    tibble(N = nrow(.x), N_complete = sum(complete.cases(items)), alpha = alpha)
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(N), Country)

saveRDS(AOT_alpha_country, file.path(v2_dir, "derived", "aot-alpha-by-country.rds"))
knitr::kable(
  filter(AOT_alpha_country, N >= 100), digits = 2,
  col.names = c("Country", "N", "Complete-item N", "Cronbach's alpha"),
  caption = "Internal consistency of the Actively Open-Minded Thinking scale by country (N ≥ 100)."
)
```

Among countries shown, AOT alpha ranges from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(AOT_alpha_country$alpha[AOT_alpha_country$N >= 100], na.rm = TRUE))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(AOT_alpha_country$alpha[AOT_alpha_country$N >= 100], na.rm = TRUE))`. These pooled item-consistency estimates do not test whether item loadings or intercepts are comparable across countries.

```{r v2-chunk-044, echo=FALSE}

AOT_items <- paste0("AOT_", 1:13)

country_N <- table(d$Country)
countries_MI <- names(country_N[country_N >= 100])

d_AOT_MI <- d %>%
  filter(Country %in% countries_MI)

AOT_model <- '
  AOT =~ AOT_1 + AOT_2 + AOT_3 + AOT_4 + AOT_5 +
         AOT_6 + AOT_7 + AOT_8 + AOT_9 + AOT_10 +
         AOT_11 + AOT_12 + AOT_13

  NEG =~ AOT_2 + AOT_4 + AOT_5 + AOT_6 +
         AOT_7 + AOT_8 + AOT_10 + AOT_13

  AOT ~~ 0*NEG
  NEG ~~ 1*NEG
'

AOT_NEG_items <- c(
  "AOT_2", "AOT_4", "AOT_5", "AOT_6",
  "AOT_7", "AOT_8", "AOT_10", "AOT_13"
)

AOT_method_loadings <- paste0("NEG=~", AOT_NEG_items)

fit_AOT_config <- v2_fit(cfa(
  AOT_model,
  data = d_AOT_MI,
  group = "Country",
  estimator = "MLR",
  std.lv = TRUE,
  missing = "listwise"
))

fit_AOT_metric <- v2_fit(cfa(
  AOT_model,
  data = d_AOT_MI,
  group = "Country",
  estimator = "MLR",
  std.lv = TRUE,
  missing = "listwise",
  group.equal = "loadings",
  group.partial = AOT_method_loadings
))

fit_AOT_scalar <- v2_fit(cfa(
  AOT_model,
  data = d_AOT_MI,
  group = "Country",
  estimator = "MLR",
  std.lv = TRUE,
  missing = "listwise",
  group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"),
  group.partial = AOT_method_loadings
))

get_MI_fit <- function(fit) {
  fitMeasures(
    fit,
    c(
      "cfi.robust",
      "tli.robust",
      "rmsea.robust",
      "srmr"
    )
  )
}

fits_AOT <- rbind(
  Configural = get_MI_fit(fit_AOT_config),
  Metric     = get_MI_fit(fit_AOT_metric),
  Scalar     = get_MI_fit(fit_AOT_scalar)
)

saveRDS(
  list(
    fits_AOT = fits_AOT,
    fit_AOT_config = fit_AOT_config,
    fit_AOT_metric = fit_AOT_metric,
    fit_AOT_scalar = fit_AOT_scalar
  ),
  file = file.path(v2_dir, "derived", "AOT_measurement_invariance.rds")
)

The AOT model separates substantive AOT from the negative-wording factor. The method factor’s variance is fixed to one in every country to identify its scale while its loadings remain free. Robust CFI is `r sprintf("%.3f", fits_AOT["Configural", "cfi.robust"])` configural; metric and scalar ΔCFI are `r sprintf("%.3f", fits_AOT["Metric", "cfi.robust"] - fits_AOT["Configural", "cfi.robust"])` and `r sprintf("%.3f", fits_AOT["Scalar", "cfi.robust"] - fits_AOT["Metric", "cfi.robust"])`. The accompanying diagnostics show whether the fits are admissible before interpreting the change indices.


#### Individualistic and collectivistic cultural tendencies scale

The 16 items are specified as four correlated factors: horizontal and vertical individualism, and horizontal and vertical collectivism. The analysis retains the 200-participant country threshold because earlier fits with smaller country samples produced inadmissible solutions; the diagnostics below evaluate the refitted models on the current preregistered exclusion sample.

```{r v2-chunk-046}

IC_model <- '
  HI =~ IC_1 + IC_2 + IC_3 + IC_4
  VI =~ IC_5 + IC_6 + IC_7 + IC_8
  HC =~ IC_9 + IC_10 + IC_11 + IC_12
  VC =~ IC_13 + IC_14 + IC_15 + IC_16'

  filter(Country %in% countries_MI)

The configural fit indices summarize how well the four-factor structure represents the data across included countries. ### Individual differences and corrective behaviour (preregistered exploratory analyses)

```{r v2-chunk-049}
ind_diff_vars <- c(
  "IH_score",
  "AOT_score",
  "IC_HI",
  "IC_VI",
  "IC_HC",
  "IC_VC"
)

cor_mat <- cor(
  d[, ind_diff_vars],
  use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
  method = "pearson"
)

knitr::kable(
  round(cor_mat, 2),
  caption = "Correlations between individual-difference measures"
)
```

The correlation table gives the pairwise-complete Pearson associations among the individual-difference measures. It is descriptive and does not adjust for country or test whether any measure predicts correction.


```{r v2-chunk-050}
dat_H1 <- dat_H1 %>%
  mutate(IH_score = scale(IH_score),
         AOT_score = scale(AOT_score),
         IC_HI = scale(IC_HI),
         IC_VI = scale(IC_VI),
         IC_HC = scale(IC_HC),
         IC_VC = scale(IC_VC))

dat_Hother <- dat_Hother %>%
  mutate(IH_score = scale(IH_score),
         AOT_score = scale(AOT_score),
         IC_HI = scale(IC_HI),
         IC_VI = scale(IC_VI),
         IC_HC = scale(IC_HC),
         IC_VC = scale(IC_VC))

mH1_exploi <- v2_fit(glmer(
  correct_phase2 ~ (feedback * justification) *
    (IH_score + AOT_score + IC_HI + IC_VI + IC_HC + IC_VC) +
    (feedback * justification || Country) + (1 | problem),
  family = binomial("logit"), data = dat_H1,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))
))
m_all_exploi <- v2_fit(glmer(
  corrected ~ (feedback * justification) *
    (IH_score + AOT_score + IC_HI + IC_VI + IC_HC + IC_VC) +
    (feedback * justification || Country) + (1 | problem),
  family = binomial("logit"), data = dat_Hother,
  control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))
))
```


```{r v2-chunk-051}
model_table_2(mH1_exploi, caption="Model for H1, including all individual differences measures as predictors.")
```

\newpage


```{r v2-chunk-052}
model_table_2(m_all_exploi, caption="Model for H2-H3, including all individual differences measures as predictors.")
```

These multivariable models estimate associations between standardized individual-difference scores and the correction outcomes while including the planned country and problem random effects. Coefficients are conditional on the other scale scores in the same model.


### Individual differences and corrective behaviour (within-country centring)

Scores are centered within country so fitted coefficients use within-country variation rather than between-country differences in scale means. AOT scores are centered for completeness but are omitted from the fitted formulas in this specification; the models include IH and the four IC subscales.

```{r v2-chunk-053}

ID_vars <- c(
  "IH_score", "AOT_score",
  "IC_HI", "IC_VI", "IC_HC", "IC_VC"
)

dat_H1 <- dat_H1 %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(ID_vars),
      ~ .x - mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      .names = "{.col}_wc"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

dat_Hother <- dat_Hother %>%
  group_by(Country) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(ID_vars),
      ~ .x - mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      .names = "{.col}_wc"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

```

### Community and Student Sample Differences

The source `Sample` field contains missing and non-standard entries. The first table records the raw labels before any repair; the second locates missing or invalid labels by country and lab. For analysis, invalid labels are treated as missing and are inferred only when all valid records from the same country–lab combination identify one sample type.

```{r v2-chunk-057, echo=FALSE}
sample_raw_counts <- d %>%
  mutate(Sample_raw = if_else(is.na(Sample), "(Missing)", as.character(Sample))) %>%
  count(Sample_raw, name = "Participants", sort = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(Percent = 100 * Participants / sum(Participants))
knitr::kable(sample_raw_counts, digits = 1,
             col.names = c("Raw sample value", "Participants", "Percent"),
             caption = "Raw values in the Sample field after the preregistered exclusions.")

sample_by_culture <- d %>%
  mutate(Sample_raw = if_else(is.na(Sample), "(Missing)", as.character(Sample))) %>%
  count(culture, Sample_raw, name = "Participants") %>%
  group_by(culture) %>%
  mutate(Percent = 100 * Participants / sum(Participants)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(culture, desc(Participants))
knitr::kable(sample_by_culture, digits = 1,
             col.names = c("Cultural group", "Raw sample value", "Participants", "Percent"),
             caption = "Raw sample labels by cultural group.")

sample_missing_labs <- d %>%
  filter(is.na(Sample) | !Sample %in% c("Student", "Community")) %>%
  group_by(Country, LabID) %>%
  summarise(Participants = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(Participants), Country, LabID)
knitr::kable(sample_missing_labs,
             caption = "Country and lab combinations with missing or invalid sample labels.")

d <- d %>%
  mutate(
    Sample = ifelse(
      Sample %in% c("Student", "Community"),
      Sample,
      NA_character_
    )
  )

d <- d %>%
  group_by(Country, LabID) %>%
  mutate(
    n_sample_types = n_distinct(Sample[!is.na(Sample)]),

    sample_inferred = ifelse(
      n_sample_types == 1,
      first(na.omit(Sample)),
      NA_character_
    ),

    Sample = coalesce(Sample, sample_inferred)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-n_sample_types, -sample_inferred)

sample_cleaned <- d %>% distinct(participant, Sample)
dat_H1 <- dat_H1 %>% select(-Sample) %>% left_join(sample_cleaned, by = "participant")
dat_Hother <- dat_Hother %>% select(-Sample) %>% left_join(sample_cleaned, by = "participant")

```

After repair, sample type is joined back to the analysis datasets by participant. The sample-type models below therefore include only records confidently classified as Student or Community; unresolved cases remain outside those comparisons.

```{r v2-chunk-058}
mH1_explo_sampletype <- v2_fit(glmer(correct_phase2 ~ (feedback * justification)*Sample +
   (feedback * justification||Country)+ (1|problem),
   family = binomial("logit"), data = dat_H1, #[is.element(dat_H1$Sample, c("Student", "Community")),],
   subset = Sample %in% c("Student", "Community"),
   control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa",
      optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))

m_all_explo_sampletype <- v2_fit(glmer(corrected ~ (feedback * justification)*Sample +
   (feedback * justification||Country)+ (1|problem),
   family = binomial("logit"),
   data = dat_Hother, # [is.element(dat_Hother$Sample, c("Student", "Community")),],
   subset = Sample %in% c("Student", "Community"),
   control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa",
     optCtrl = list(maxfun = 1e5))))
```

      k = c(7, 5),
      bs = c("cr", "tp")),
  data = tab_calib,
  method = "REML"
))

m_calib_ref <- v2_fit(gam(
  calib_ref ~
    s(accuracy_reflective, k = 7, bs = "cr") +
    s(IH_z, k = 5) +
    ti(
      accuracy_reflective,

make_predictions <- function(model, accuracy_var, phase) {

  newdat <- expand_grid(
    accuracy = seq(0, 6, length.out = 121),
    IH_z = c(-1, 0, 1)
  )

  names(newdat)[names(newdat) == "accuracy"] <- accuracy_var

  pr <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = newdat,
    type = "response",
    se.fit = TRUE
  )

  newdat %>%
    mutate(
      fit = as.numeric(pr$fit),
      se = as.numeric(pr$se.fit),
      lower = fit - 1.96 * se,
      upper = fit + 1.96 * se,

      IH = factor(
        IH_z,
        levels = c(-1, 0, 1),
        labels = c(
          "IH: -1 SD",
          "IH: mean",
          "IH: +1 SD"
        )
      ),

      Phase = phase,

      accuracy = .data[[accuracy_var]]
    ) %>%
    select(
      accuracy, IH_z, IH,
      fit, lower, upper, Phase
    )
}

pred_int <- make_predictions(
  m_calib_int,
  "accuracy_intuitive",
  "Intuitive phase"
)

pred_ref <- make_predictions(
  m_calib_ref,
  "accuracy_reflective",
  "Reflective phase"
)

pred_calib <- bind_rows(
  pred_int,
  pred_ref
)

```{r v2-chunk-063, echo=FALSE}
format_p <- function(p, digits = 3) {
  case_when(
    is.na(p)  ~ "",
    p < 0.001 ~ "< .001",
    TRUE      ~ sub("^0", "", sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), p))
  )
}

gam_model_table <- function(models,
                            caption = NULL,
                            model_labels = NULL,
                            term_labels = NULL,
                            digits = 3) {

  if (inherits(models, "gam")) {
    models <- list(Model = models)
  }

  if (is.null(names(models)) || any(names(models) == "")) {
    names(models) <- paste0("Model ", seq_along(models))
  }

  if (!is.null(model_labels)) {
    ii <- match(names(models), names(model_labels))
    names(models)[!is.na(ii)] <- model_labels[ii[!is.na(ii)]]
  }

  tab <- imap_dfr(models, function(model, model_name) {

    param <- broom::tidy(
      model,
      parametric = TRUE
    ) %>%
      transmute(
        Model = model_name,
        Component = "Parametric",
        Term = term,
        Estimate = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), estimate),
        SE = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), std.error),
        edf = "",
        `Ref. df` = "",
        Statistic = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), statistic),
        p = format_p(p.value, digits)
      )

    smooth <- broom::tidy(
      model,
      parametric = FALSE
    ) %>%
      transmute(
        Model = model_name,
        Component = "Smooth",
        Term = term,
        Estimate = "",
        SE = "",
        edf = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), edf),
        `Ref. df` = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), ref.df),
        Statistic = sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), statistic),
        p = format_p(p.value, digits)
      )

    bind_rows(param, smooth)
  })

  if (!is.null(term_labels)) {
    ii <- match(tab$Term, names(term_labels))
    tab$Term[!is.na(ii)] <- term_labels[ii[!is.na(ii)]]
  }

  knitr::kable(
    tab,
    format = "pipe",
    align = c("l", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
    caption = caption
  )
}
```

#### Binned observations for the calibration plots

The additional plot versions overlay participant-level mean estimates of performance, with **±1 standard error** bars. Only participants with complete data for the relevant phase and IH contribute to a bin. Accuracy levels **1–6** are displayed, giving 12 median-split points or 30 quintile points per phase; zero-correct observations remain in the fitted models and original plots.

For the accuracy-axis plots, one median IH cutoff is calculated across participants in the calibration dataset and used for both phases and every accuracy level. Scores equal to the median belong to the lower group, so ties may make the group sizes unequal. Point shapes distinguish these two observed groups; the original three curves still show predictions at mean IH and ±1 SD, rather than predictions averaged over the median-split groups.

For the IH-axis plots, participants are sorted by IH within each phase and accuracy level and divided into five bins with counts differing by at most one. Ties in IH are ordered by participant ID and may span bins. Points are placed at each bin’s mean IH and mean estimated performance, and their colours match the corresponding accuracy curves. Error bars describe variability across participant estimates; they are distinct from the model confidence bands.

```{r calibration-observation-bins}
calib_IH_median <- median(tab_calib$IH_score[is.finite(tab_calib$IH_z)], na.rm = TRUE)
calib_observed <- bind_rows(
  tab_calib %>% transmute(participant, IH_score, IH_z,
    Phase = "Intuitive phase", accuracy = accuracy_intuitive, estimate = calib_int),
  tab_calib %>% transmute(participant, IH_score, IH_z,
    Phase = "Reflective phase", accuracy = accuracy_reflective, estimate = calib_ref)
) %>%
  filter(is.finite(estimate), is.finite(IH_score), is.finite(IH_z), accuracy %in% 1:6) %>%
  mutate(
    IH_group = factor(if_else(IH_score <= calib_IH_median,
      "At/below IH median", "Above IH median"),
      levels = c("At/below IH median", "Above IH median")),
    accuracy_level = factor(accuracy, levels = 1:6)
  )

calib_bins_median <- calib_observed %>%
  group_by(Phase, accuracy, IH_group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), IH_mean = mean(IH_score), mean_estimate = mean(estimate),
            se = sd(estimate) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")

calib_quintile_membership <- calib_observed %>%
  arrange(Phase, accuracy, IH_score, participant) %>%
  group_by(Phase, accuracy, accuracy_level) %>%
  mutate(IH_bin = ntile(row_number(), 5L)) %>%
  ungroup()
calib_bins_quintile <- calib_quintile_membership %>%
  group_by(Phase, accuracy, accuracy_level, IH_bin) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), IH_mean = mean(IH_score), mean_estimate = mean(estimate),
            se = sd(estimate) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")

# Fail visibly if the requested layout cannot be supported by the data.
stopifnot(all(count(calib_bins_median, Phase)$n == 12L),
          all(count(calib_bins_quintile, Phase)$n == 30L),
          all(calib_bins_median$n >= 2L), all(calib_bins_quintile$n >= 2L))
saveRDS(list(median_cutoff = calib_IH_median, median = calib_bins_median,
             quintile = calib_bins_quintile),
        file.path(v2_dir, "derived", "calibration-observed-bins.rds"))

v2_plot_calibration_bins <- function(predictions) {
  dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.16)
  ggplot(predictions, aes(accuracy, fit, colour = IH, fill = IH)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = .15, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = 2) +
    geom_errorbar(data = calib_bins_median,
      aes(x = accuracy, ymin = mean_estimate - se, ymax = mean_estimate + se,
          group = IH_group), inherit.aes = FALSE, position = dodge,
      width = .10, colour = "black", linewidth = .4) +
    geom_point(data = calib_bins_median,
      aes(x = accuracy, y = mean_estimate, shape = IH_group),
      inherit.aes = FALSE, position = dodge, colour = "black", size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~Phase, nrow = 1) +
    scale_colour_viridis_d() + scale_fill_viridis_d() +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17)) +
    coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 6), ylim = c(0, 6)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:6) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
    labs(x = "Actual accuracy", y = "Estimated number correct",
         colour = "Model IH", fill = "Model IH", shape = "Observed IH group") +
    ml_theme() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

v2_plot_ih_bins <- function(predictions, ih_column) {
  ggplot(predictions, aes(x = .data[[ih_column]], y = fit,
                         colour = accuracy_level, fill = accuracy_level)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = .12, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_errorbar(data = calib_bins_quintile,
      aes(x = IH_mean, ymin = mean_estimate - se, ymax = mean_estimate + se,
          colour = accuracy_level), inherit.aes = FALSE, width = .06, linewidth = .4) +
    geom_point(data = calib_bins_quintile,
      aes(x = IH_mean, y = mean_estimate, colour = accuracy_level),
      inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~Phase, nrow = 1) +
    scale_colour_viridis_d(drop = FALSE) + scale_fill_viridis_d(drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:6) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1, 7)) +
    labs(x = "Intellectual humility", y = "Estimated number correct",
         colour = "Actual accuracy", fill = "Actual accuracy") + ml_theme()
}

#| fig-align: 'center'

make_IH_predictions <- function(model,
                                data,
                                accuracy_var,
                                phase,
                                accuracy_values = 1:6,
                                n_IH = 200) {
  
  
  IH_seq <- (seq(1,7,length.out = n_IH) - mean(tab_calib$IH_score, na.rm = TRUE))/sd(tab_calib$IH_score, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  newdat <- expand_grid(
    IH_z = IH_seq,
    accuracy = accuracy_values
  )
  
  names(newdat)[names(newdat) == "accuracy"] <- accuracy_var
  
  pr <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = newdat,
    type = "response",
    se.fit = TRUE
  )
  
  newdat %>%
    mutate(
      fit   = as.numeric(pr$fit),
      se    = as.numeric(pr$se.fit),
      lower = fit - 1.96 * se,
      upper = fit + 1.96 * se,
      accuracy_level = factor(.data[[accuracy_var]],
                              levels = accuracy_values),
      Phase = phase
    )
}

  accuracy_var = "accuracy_intuitive",

#### Robustness analysis: quasibinomial GAMs

As a robustness analysis, we repeated the calibration analyses using quasibinomial GAMs. These models constrain predicted estimates to the possible 0–6 range while allowing for overdispersion relative to the binomial variance.

```{r}
#| label: gam-quasibinomial
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(mgcv)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

m_calib_int_qbin <- v2_fit(gam(
  cbind(calib_int, 6 - calib_int) ~
    s(accuracy_intuitive, k = 7, bs = "cr") +
    s(IH_z, k = 5) +
    ti(
      accuracy_intuitive,
      IH_z,
      k = c(7, 5),
      bs = c("cr", "tp")
    ),
  family = quasibinomial(link = "logit"),
  data = tab_calib,
  method = "REML"
))

m_calib_ref_qbin <- v2_fit(gam(
  cbind(calib_ref, 6 - calib_ref) ~
    s(accuracy_reflective, k = 7, bs = "cr") +
    s(IH_z, k = 5) +
    ti(
      accuracy_reflective,
      IH_z,
      k = c(7, 5),
      bs = c("cr", "tp")
    ),
  family = quasibinomial(link = "logit"),
  data = tab_calib,
  method = "REML"
))

```

#### Predicted calibration curves

```{r}
#| label: fig-gam-qbin-calibration
#| fig-cap: "Quasibinomial robustness analysis of intellectual humility and calibration of estimated performance. Lines show model-predicted estimates at the mean and ±1 SD of intellectual humility; shaded bands indicate 95% confidence intervals. The dashed diagonal indicates perfect calibration."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-align: 'center'

make_qbin_calib_predictions <- function(model,
                                        accuracy_var,
                                        phase) {

  newdat <- expand_grid(
    accuracy = seq(0, 6, length.out = 121),
    IH_z = c(-1, 0, 1)
  )

  names(newdat)[names(newdat) == "accuracy"] <- accuracy_var

  pr <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = newdat,
    type = "link",
    se.fit = TRUE
  )

  newdat %>%
    mutate(
      eta = as.numeric(pr$fit),
      se = as.numeric(pr$se.fit),

      fit   = 6 * plogis(eta),
      lower = 6 * plogis(eta - 1.96 * se),
      upper = 6 * plogis(eta + 1.96 * se),

      IH = factor(
        IH_z,
        levels = c(-1, 0, 1),
        labels = c(
          "IH: -1 SD",
          "IH: mean",
          "IH: +1 SD"
        )
      ),

      Phase = phase,
      accuracy = .data[[accuracy_var]]
    ) %>%
    select(
      accuracy, IH_z, IH,
      fit, lower, upper, Phase
    )
}

pred_qbin_int <- make_qbin_calib_predictions(
  m_calib_int_qbin,
  "accuracy_intuitive",
  "Intuitive phase"
)

pred_qbin_ref <- make_qbin_calib_predictions(
  m_calib_ref_qbin,
  "accuracy_reflective",
  "Reflective phase"
)

pred_qbin_calib <- bind_rows(
  pred_qbin_int,
  pred_qbin_ref
)

ggplot(

    x = accuracy,

  )
) +

  geom_abline(
    intercept = 0,
    slope = 1,
    linetype = 2
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Phase, nrow = 1) +
  coord_equal(
    xlim = c(0, 6),
    ylim = c(0, 6)
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_d()+
  scale_fill_viridis_d()+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
  labs(
    x = "Actual accuracy",

Curves and bands retain the original mean/±1 SD IH predictions and pointwise 95% confidence intervals. Black point shapes indicate the two observed IH groups; bars show ±1 SE. Points are slightly dodged horizontally for visibility."

v2_plot_calibration_bins(pred_qbin_calib)

#### Intellectual humility interaction plots

```{r}
#| label: fig-gam-qbin-IH
#| fig-cap: "Quasibinomial robustness analysis of intellectual humility, actual accuracy, and estimated performance. Lines show model-predicted estimates across the observed range of intellectual humility scores, separately for each level of actual accuracy; shaded bands indicate 95% confidence intervals."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-align: 'center'

IH_mean <- mean(tab_calib$IH_score, na.rm = TRUE)
IH_sd   <- sd(tab_calib$IH_score, na.rm = TRUE)

make_qbin_IH_predictions <- function(model,
                                     data,
                                     accuracy_var,
                                     phase,
                                     accuracy_values = 1:6,
                                     n_IH = 200) {

  IH_raw <- seq(
    min(data$IH_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(data$IH_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    length.out = n_IH
  )

  newdat <- expand_grid(
    IH_score = IH_raw,
    accuracy = accuracy_values
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      IH_z = (IH_score - IH_mean) / IH_sd
    )

  names(newdat)[names(newdat) == "accuracy"] <- accuracy_var

  pr <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = newdat,
    type = "link",
    se.fit = TRUE
  )

  newdat %>%
    mutate(
      eta = as.numeric(pr$fit),
      se = as.numeric(pr$se.fit),

      fit   = 6 * plogis(eta),
      lower = 6 * plogis(eta - 1.96 * se),
      upper = 6 * plogis(eta + 1.96 * se),

      accuracy_level = factor(
        .data[[accuracy_var]],
        levels = accuracy_values
      ),

      Phase = phase
    )
}

pred_qbin_IH_int <- make_qbin_IH_predictions(
  model = m_calib_int_qbin,
  data = tab_calib,
  accuracy_var = "accuracy_intuitive",
  phase = "Intuitive phase"
)

pred_qbin_IH_ref <- make_qbin_IH_predictions(
  model = m_calib_ref_qbin,
  data = tab_calib,
  accuracy_var = "accuracy_reflective",
  phase = "Reflective phase"
)

pred_qbin_IH <- bind_rows(
  pred_qbin_IH_int,
  pred_qbin_IH_ref
)

ggplot(
  pred_qbin_IH,
  aes(
    x = IH_score,
    y = fit,
    colour = accuracy_level,
    fill = accuracy_level
  )
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    alpha = 0.12,
    colour = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~Phase, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = 0:6
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_d()+
  scale_fill_viridis_d()+
  labs(
    x = "Intellectual humility",
    y = "Predicted estimate of accuracy",
    colour = "Actual accuracy",
    fill = "Actual accuracy"
  ) +
  ml_theme()
